arxiv-2208-01345.title: Studying large-scale structure probes of modified gravity with COLA
arxiv-2208-01345.creator: Albert Izard
arxiv-2208-01345.description: Abstract We study the effect of two Modified Gravity (MG) theories, f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) and nDGP, on three probes of large-scale structure, the real space power spectrum estimator Q 0 Q_{0} , bispectrum and voids, and validate fast approximate COLA simulations against full N -body simulations for the prediction of these probes.

arxiv-2212-10298.title: Plasmons in a Square of Two-Dimensional Electrons
arxiv-2212-10298.creator: A. M. Zarezin a,b , D. Mylnikov b , A. S. Petrov b , D. Svintsov b , P. A. Gusikhin a , I. V. Kukushkin a , V. M. Muravev a
arxiv-2212-10298.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by A. M. Zarezin a,b , D. Mylnikov b , A. S. Petrov b , D. Svintsov b , P. A. Gusikhin a , I. V. Kukushkin a , V. M. Muravev a. Microwave absorption spectra of a single square of two-dimensional electrons (2DES) have been investigated using an optical detection technique. Fundamental dipole and harmonic quadrupole plasmon modes have been identified and compared to those in the disk geometry.

Let 𝒪 ​ 𝒢 ⁡ ( 4 ) \OG(4) denote the family of all graph-group pairs ( Γ , G ) (\Gamma,G) where Γ \Gamma is finite, 4-valent, connected, and G G -oriented ( G G -half-arc-transitive). A subfamily of 𝒪 ​ 𝒢 ⁡ ( 4 ) \OG(4) has recently been identified as ‘basic’ in the sense that all graphs in this family are normal covers of at least one basic member.

arxiv-2503-04276.title: Soft X-ray imaging with coherence tomography in the water window spectral range using high-harmonic generation
arxiv-2503-04276.creator: Julius Reinhard , 1,2*,† Felix Wiesner , 1,2,† Themistoklis Sidiropoulos , 3 Martin Hennecke , 3 Sophia Kaleta , 1,2 Julian Späthe , 1 Johann Jakob Abel, 1 Martin Wünsche , 1,2,4 Gabriele Schmidl, 5 Jonathan Plentz , 5 Uwe Hübner, 5 Katharina Freiberg , 6 Jonathan Apell, 6,7 Stephanie Lippmann , 8 M
arxiv-2503-04276.description: Abstract Abstract High-harmonic generation (HHG) is used as a source for various imaging applications in the extreme ultraviolet spectral range. It offers spatially coherent radiation and unique elemental contrast with the potential for attosecond time resolution. The unfavorable efficiency scaling to higher photon energies prevented the imaging application in the soft X-ray range so far.

arxiv-2510-17755.title: Mott vs Kondo: Influence of Various Density Functional Based Methods on the Ce Isostructural Phase Transition Mechanism
arxiv-2510-17755.creator: Brenden W. Hamilton, Alexander R. Muñoz, Travis E. Jones, Benjamin T. Nebgen
arxiv-2510-17755.description: Abstract The cerium iso-structural phase transition ( γ \gamma to α \alpha ) is dominated by f-electron localization changes that results in a magnetic ordering change and a volume collapse. Generally, these physics are difficult to capture with ab initio and first principles methods.

arxiv-2511-08170.title: Distributed Zero-Shot Learning for Visual Recognition
arxiv-2511-08170.creator: Zhi Chen, Yadan Luo, Zi Huang, Jingjing Li, Sen Wang, Xin Yu
arxiv-2511-08170.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a Distributed Zero-Shot Learning (DistZSL) framework that can fully exploit decentralized data to learn an effective model for unseen classes. Considering the data heterogeneity issues across distributed nodes, we introduce two key components to ensure the effective learning of DistZSL: a cross-node attribute regularizer and a global attribute-to-visual consensus.

arxiv-2512-12251.title: Mutual-visibility coloring of graphs
arxiv-2512-12251.creator: Saneesh Babu, Gabriele Di Stefano, Aparna Lakshmanan S
arxiv-2512-12251.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Saneesh Babu, Gabriele Di Stefano, Aparna Lakshmanan S. The mutual-visibility chromatic number of a graph G G is the smallest number of colors needed to color the vertices of G G such that each color class is a mutual-visibility set. In this paper, we prove that determining the mutual-visibility chromatic number of a graph is NP-complete even when restricted to the class of graphs having diameter four and mutual-visibility chromatic number two.

pmc-11445694.creator: Diana Papaioannou, Sienna Hamer-Kiwacz, Cara Mooney, Kirsty Sprange, Cindy Cooper, Alicia O’Cathain

pmc-12405370.title: The use of stem cells and organoids for modeling host-microbe interactions in low-biomass tissues
pmc-12405370.creator: Claire A. Shaw, Margo Verstrate, Kinga Graniczkowska, Katie R. Risoen, Pouya Dini, Bart C. Weimer
pmc-12405370.description: Stem cells and organoids have emerged as pivotal biological tools for biologically relevant models. Together, these in vitro models realistically recapitulate structural and functional elements of the in vivo organ, allowing for studies of cellular, molecular, and genetic features that underpin various diseases that are difficult to observe in low-biomass tissues.

pmc-12468638.title: Cervical Cancer Screening in Refugee and Migrant Populations: Results of Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis in Cross-Sectional and Cohort Studies
pmc-12468638.creator: Vincenzo Restivo, Davide Graci, Angelo Immordino, Daniele Giacomo Mancuso, Fátima Morales, Chiara Pace, Alessandra Pirrello, Alessandra Casuccio, Palmira Immordino, Riffat Mehboob
pmc-12468638.description: Simple SummaryCervical cancer is one of the most common cancers in women, but it can often be prevented through vaccination and regular screening tests. Unfortunately, not all groups of women benefit equally from these prevention programs. Migrant and refugee women, in particular, may face cultural, financial, and social barriers that make it harder for them to access screening.

pmc-12611966.title: Multi-omics analysis revealed potential use of immunotherapy and CDK4/6 inhibitors in intimal sarcoma
pmc-12611966.creator: Bei Wang, Rongrong Chen, Huan Yin, Ziyi Chang, Yao Liu, Dingrong Zhong, Feng Li
pmc-12611966.description: BackgroundIntimal sarcoma (IS) and angiosarcoma (AS), two rare yet highly aggressive vascular mesenchymal malignancies, present significant therapeutic challenges due to their scarcity, which underscoring the urgent need to investigate genetic alterations and tumor microenvironment (TME) features for novel therapeutic development.

pmc-12639388.title: Natural compounds modulating redox metabolism and Inflammation: New insights in skin cancer prevention and therapy
pmc-12639388.creator: Sinemyiz Atalay Ekiner, Agnieszka Gęgotek, Elżbieta Skrzydlewska
pmc-12639388.description: UV radiation penetrating human skin causes DNA damages, including specific mutations, redox imbalances, oxidative damage to macromolecules, and consequently changes in intracellular signaling pathways, particularly those involved in inflammation, cell differentiation, and survival. These metabolic changes may ultimately contribute to the development of skin cancers, including melanoma, the most lethal form, as well as other types of skin cancer.

pmc-12811810.title: Effects of Oral and Maxillofacial Trauma on Soft Tissue Esthetic Outcomes of Dental Implants: A Systematic Review
pmc-12811810.creator: Ali Y Alameri, Sarah F Altukruni, Mahdi Saileek, Ali A Alrakah, Abdullah Khalid A Alhamwan, Dhaifallah I Alzahrani, Alaa A Alsubki, Laila Alanaz
pmc-12811810.description: Oral and maxillofacial trauma frequently results in the loss of anterior teeth and disruption of the surrounding soft and hard tissues, creating significant challenges for implant rehabilitation in esthetically sensitive areas. Achieving stable peri-implant soft tissue contours is essential for long-term esthetic success, yet the influence of prior trauma on soft tissue outcomes remains unclear.

pmc-13181181.title: Quality of Life After Cardiac Surgery: The QUACS Study and Benefit Prediction Model
pmc-13181181.creator: Samer A M Nashef, James Willard, Christine Mills, Yi-Da Chiu, Philip Noyes, Michael C Petch, Dominique-Laurent Couturier, Stephen R Large
pmc-13181181.description: ObjectivesSafer cardiac surgery is being offered to more high-risk and frail patients, improving both survival and quality of life (QoL) for most. The QoL After Cardiac Surgery Study (QUACS) evaluated QoL changes postoperatively to identify those who do not benefit from and may be harmed by intervention.MethodsModerate- and high-risk cardiac surgery patients enrolled in a prospective, national multicentre study (2019-2023).

pmc-13200352.title: Enhanced corn leaf disease detection using sharpness-aware minimization optimized CNNs
pmc-13200352.creator: Manoj Kumar Sharma, Richa Sharma, Gireesh Kumar
pmc-13200352.description: Crop diseases significantly threaten global food security by directly affecting the crop yield and quality. The traditional diagnostic methods are labour intensive and human error prone. However, the existing deep learning solutions suffer with poor generalization due to the sharp loss landscapes. The proposed work addresses this limitation and optimizes the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) using the Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM).

pmc-13372729.title: A multidrug-resistant organism tracking and alert system is associated with lower MRSA and CP-CRE infection rates at Veterans Affairs Medical Centers
pmc-13372729.creator: Amanda Vivo, Cara Ray, Tarek El Ali, Geneva M. Wilson, Reside Jacob, Makoto M. Jones, Natalie R. Hicks, Christopher D. Pfeiffer, Charlesnika T. Evans
pmc-13372729.description: This study investigates Veterans Affairs Bug Alert (VABA) usage on methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and carbapenemase-producing carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CP-CRE) infection rates in VA facilities. Significant association between increased VABA use and decreased MRSA and CP-CRE infection rates supports VABA as part of infection control strategies.

pmc-13631370.title: Presynaptic accumulation of APP-CTFβ may contribute to synaptic dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-13631370.creator: Akshay Kapadia, Fabian Schuhmann, Ezgi Daskin, Jochen Walter, Isabell Lindahl, Neda Rahmani, Tjado H J Morrema, Annemieke J M Rozemuller, Baayla D C Boon, Weria Pezeshkian, Anne-Sophie Hafner
pmc-13631370.description: The study of Alzheimer’s disease (AD)-associated mutations has implicated dysregulation of amyloid precursor protein (APP) proteolysis in the disease. Brain recordings have revealed synaptic hyperexcitation during asymptomatic and early stages of AD, reverting to overinhibition as dementia progresses. Here, we show that endogenous APP and its proteolytic C-terminal fragments (APP-CTFs), the precursors of amyloid-β (Aβ), are enriched at excitatory synapses.
